newsitem.title: USA: WHX says tentative pact could end strike.
newsitem.headline: WHX says tentative pact could end strike.

text.p: Wheeling-Pittsburgh Corp and the United Steelworkers of America said on Friday they had reached a tentative agreement that could end a 10-month strike.
"The tentative agreement will be submitted to the local union presidents for their action and to the members for ratification," the two parties said in a statement.
Terms of the accord were not disclosed.
Some 4,500 union workers have been on strike since last October, idling eight steel plants in Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio.

The dispute centers on pensions, with the union demanding that Wheeling-Pittsburgh's parent company, WHX Corp, establish a defined benefit plan and the company holding that it cannot afford to meet the demand.
